title: Dependencies and Package Management
learningObjectives: Update dependencies with compatibility and security in mind
Remove unused packages and avoid unnecessary additions

understand.concept: A dependency is software a project relies on. Package managers help discover, install, update, and record dependencies. Projects should understand what they add, use trusted sources, pin or constrain versions appropriately, review updates, and avoid unnecessary packages. Dependency files and lockfiles serve different roles depending on the ecosystem.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable workflow and collaboration practices help people coordinate changes, manage risks, and maintain a working project.
understand.analogy: A shared team task benefits when each person understands their responsibility and the agreed steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Development tools and version histories have technical behaviors that this teamwork analogy does not capture.

explain.narrative:
A dependency is software a project relies on. Package managers help discover, install, update, and record dependencies. Projects should understand what they add, use trusted sources, pin or constrain versions appropriately, review updates, and avoid unnecessary packages. Dependency files and lockfiles serve different roles depending on the ecosystem.

Use these practices as a practical guide, adapting them to the repository, language, team, and risk level. Make the intended changes visible and verify them rather than relying on assumptions.
